# Garmin Connect library notes

This project uses the third-party `garminconnect` Python library to read Garmin
Connect data. It is not an official Garmin API client. The library depends on
Garmin's web/mobile authentication and Connect API endpoints, so Garmin-side
changes, bot protection, MFA, token rules, or rate limits can break our job even
when our project code did not change.

Useful references:

- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/garminconnect/
- GitHub: https://github.com/cyberjunky/python-garminconnect
- Related issue pattern: https://github.com/cyberjunky/python-garminconnect/issues/337

## 2026-07-20

### Problem

The job runs locally from the `Sandbox` Conda environment after updating the
Garmin password, but GitHub Actions fails during Garmin login with:

```text
too many 429 error responses
```

The failure happens at Garmin's OAuth/preauthorized login step from the
GitHub-hosted runner. This suggests Garmin is rate-limiting or blocking the
cloud runner login flow. Waiting overnight did not resolve it.

### Direction

We want GitHub Actions to avoid a fresh Garmin username/password login each day.
The preferred direction is to use Garmin saved tokens/session storage:

1. Create/refresh Garmin tokens locally where login works.
2. Store the token data safely in GitHub Secrets.
3. Restore token files in GitHub Actions before the daily job runs.
4. Let `garminconnect` load/refresh tokens instead of doing a fresh login.

Token generation should normally be a one-time setup step. The daily GitHub job
should reuse the saved tokenstore and let the library refresh tokens when
possible. We should only regenerate tokens locally and update the GitHub Secret
if Garmin invalidates the saved tokens, the account security state changes, or
the tokenstore stops working.

### Changes started on branch

Branch: `garmin-token-session-auth`

- Bumped `garminconnect` from `0.2.25` to `0.3.6`.
- Added a small Garmin authentication helper in `daily_jobs/help_functions.py`.
- The helper uses the `GARMINTOKENS` environment variable when present.
- Wired the daily statistics job to use the helper.
- Created a project-specific local Conda environment: `trainingpeaks_customlog`.
- Installed project requirements in that environment and verified
  `garminconnect 0.3.6` imports successfully.
- Updated `.vscode/settings.json` so VS Code and Code Runner use
  `trainingpeaks_customlog` instead of the older shared `Sandbox` environment.
- Added `daily_jobs/create_garmin_tokens.py` for local tokenstore creation in
  `.garminconnect`.
- Local token generation created `.garminconnect/garmin_tokens.json`.
- GitHub Actions should restore this file from a secret named
  `GARMIN_TOKENS_JSON` and set `GARMINTOKENS=.garminconnect` before running the
  job.
